title: Telemetry Surgeon: trace-anchor enrichment and paging-sandbox for adaptive SLOs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Our current SLO and paging system struggles to attribute short, high-amplitude latency spikes to the correct service boundary when spans are sparse or overly aggregated. This causes noisy burn-rate alerts and unnecessary oncall pages for infra teams. Goal: introduce a scoped 'trace-anchor' enrichment pipeline (Telemetry Surgeon) that attaches a small, high-fidelity tracing footprint to representative requests, improves metric alignment for short tail latency, and powers a paging-sandbox feature that lets ops test adaptive paging policies without affecting live escalation paths. Scope: - lightweight trace-anchor instrumentation in 3 candidate services (api-gateway, request-router, request-proxy) - enrichment pipeline that attaches anchor metadata to existing trace/metric events (span.labels, sampling hints) - schema extension for telemetry to carry anchor_id, anchor_class, and sample_reason - a safe paging-sandbox controller in Console that lets PMs/Oncall create simulated burn-rate scenarios and preview what pages would fire (no real pages during sandbox) - anomaly detection tuning using anchored traces to improve attribution and reduce false positives Out-of-scope: full platform sampling redesign, changes to central SLO definitions (we will surface recommendations only). Implementation plan: 1) Prototype trace-anchor injection (feature-flagged) in a canary service with 1% sampling. 2) Build enrichment transformer in observability-ingest that copies anchor metadata to metric and log events and creates TTL-limited anchor records. 3) Add anchor-aware aggregation rules in SLO pipeline so short-window p50/p95/p99 slices can consult anchor records for attribution. 4) Implement paging-sandbox UI that consumes SLO pipeline decisions but never escalates (UI + simulated pager preview). 5) Run 2-week pilot, gather precision/recall vs current alerting, tune anomaly detector thresholds. Trade-offs and constraints: - Anchors increase ingest cardinality; capped TTL and sampling mitigate cost. - We choose out-of-band anchor records rather than expanding existing spans to minimize cross-service schema churn. - Early rollout will restrict anchors to internal traffic flags to avoid customer PII leakage. Success metrics: - 40% reduction in pages caused by false-positive burn-rate alerts for the pilot services. - Improved attribution rate: proportion of burn events with a top-1 suspect microservice increases from ~54% to >80% within test windows. - No more than 5% increase in observability ingestion cost for pilot services. Rollout and rollback: feature flags at service level; ingest transformer also feature-flagged; paging-sandbox disabled until pilot auto-metrics are green; immediate rollback by disabling service-level flag if error budget is breached or errors > 0.5% of requests. Coordination: partner with Platform SRE (for paging policy logic), Console UX (sandbox UI), Security (PII audit), and Observability infra (ingest transformer). Deliverables: design doc, PoC, ingest transformer PR, SLO pipeline changes, sandbox UI prototype, pilot report with metrics and recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Trace-anchor can be enabled via a service feature flag and emits anchor_id to span metadata for sampled requests
Ingest transformer persists anchor records and copies anchor metadata to metric/log envelopes within TTL
SLO pipeline uses anchor records to tag short-window latency anomalies with candidate root cause service at >80% top-1 attribution in pilot
Paging-sandbox UI replicates the SLO evaluation path and shows simulated pages without sending real pages; sandbox runs for a simulated time window
Pilot report includes ingestion cost delta, page reduction %, attribution improvement, and safety checklist (PII, performance)
notes: Design option A: embed anchor fields directly into spans vs option B: create separate anchor record stream. Chosen: option B to avoid schema churn and reduce downstream impact.
Sampling strategy: start with 1% of requests for gateway and 0.5% for downstream services; ramp cautiously if metrics acceptable.
Retention/TTL: anchor records will have 15-minute TTL to cover typical SLO windows for burn-rate detection; revisit after pilot.
Cost mitigation: compress anchor records, strip non-essential attributes, and route anchors through a low-cost storage tier for ephemeral queries.

Security: ensure anchor payloads are scrubbed of user PII; Security review required for payload schema even though full review flagged false for scheduling reasons — schedule follow-up audit before beta rollout.
